agree.reason: It opens with Dana's own $600K figure, and the cost-vs-value maths plus the one-site pilot ask make a reply easy, though the IT-director worry gets only one line near the end.

honest.reason: Every number checks against the brief: 53% is more than half, $75K is right, $300K is slightly understated, and 21% is right; it leaves out that only two of six customers have measured results, but it does show the weaker case.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the annual cost for five sites, the dollar value of a halving on her figure, and that even the weaker 21% result pays for itself, all from the brief's numbers and in their strongest true form.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is her own stated $600K a year in returns, which carries on if nothing changes; this is implied clearly rather than stated, and the brief gives no trend for it.

qualification.reason: Giving the 21% result as a floor next to the halving is a fair, checkable hedge, but it has no timeframe for when results would show at her sites and no measure for judging the pilot.

objections.reason: The 'sits on top, doesn't replace' line and the single-site pilot partly answer the IT director's resistance, but the line comes late and doesn't say how little it asks of IT or of the system he rolled out.

fit.reason: It is short, the paragraphs fit a phone screen, the subject line is concrete, and it ends with a single clear ask, as the brief requested.
